entries.appliesTo: any person making electioneering communications that use AI to falsely portray a candidate or elected official subject to recall; persons other than candidates or committees spending over $1,000 on electioneering communications

dutySources.disclosure-ui: R.S. 18:1463(F)(1) — 'without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence'
dutySources.registration-filing: R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1) — 'Any person, other than a candidate or a committee, who makes any expenditure for … an electioneering communication shall file reports if such expenditures exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period'

sources.disclosure: R.S. 18:1463(F)(1) — 'No person shall make or cause to be made any electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that is, through the use of artificial intelligence, created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of a candidate … without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence'
sources.scope: R.S. 18:1483(33)(a) — '"Electioneering communication" means any communication, whether printed, digital, or broadcast by a media entity'
sources.penaltyMax: R.S. 18:1463(G) — 'shall be fined not more than two thousand dollars'
sources.penaltyUnit: R.S. 18:1463(G) — 'Whoever violates any provision of this Section'

flags: Criminal enforcement: violation with 'the intent to injure the reputation of a candidate or elected official subject to recall or to otherwise deceive a voter' is punishable by fine up to $2,000 'or be imprisoned, with or without hard labor, for not more than two years, or both' (R.S. 18:1463(G)); coded in election-disclosure per rule 10, fine only in penaltyMax per rule 11.
Penalty carries an intent element ('with the intent to injure the reputation … or to otherwise deceive a voter'); the disclosure duty itself in (F)(1) has no intent element.
No enforcer named in the text; penalty is criminal, so enforcement is implicitly by criminal prosecution — enforcer omitted (silence is silence).

Media-entity exemption: R.S. 18:1463(I) — 'shall not apply to a media entity that broadcasts a paid political announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication in which the broadcaster has had no input in or control over' the communication.

registration-filing duty is a general campaign-finance reporting requirement (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1), $1,000 aggregate expenditure threshold), not conditioned on AI use; included because the enacted text imposes it, but it may overstate AI-specific compliance cost.

Bill also amends non-AI campaign-finance definitions — 'contribution' (R.S. 18:1483(7)), 'coordinated expenditure' (R.S. 18:1483(8)), 'expenditure' (R.S. 18:1483(11)) — and repeals R.S. 18:1463(C)(5), 1491.7(B)(22), and 1495.5(B)(21); no coded duty/param fits these, noted here per rule 5.

'Artificial intelligence' is defined by cross-reference: R.S. 18:1463(F)(2)(a) — '"Artificial intelligence" shall have the same meaning as provided in R.S. 14:73.14'; no definition in this text (rule 4, no imports).

Disclosure form is defined by cross-reference: 'The form of the disclosure shall be consistent with the disclosure requirements of Subsection (E) of this Section' — Subsection (E) is not reproduced in this Act's text.
